summary: Jackson County, OH tower erected in 1934 with federal money and CCC labor, listed as McCune Ridge or Limerick; listed as gone, and sources disagree on agency and township.

facts.design: Aluminum-finished tower about 20 feet taller than the one on the Scioto trail, per a 1934 newspaper report
facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Ohio list of the Forest Fire Lookout Association
facts.agency: State department of forestry, built with federal funds and CCC labor (1934 report); the Forest Lookouts page lists Wayne National Forest

events.note: Erected by August 1934, per a Chillicothe Gazette report of August 15, 1934; federal funds and CCC camp labor
Allen Weese named in October 1934 as observer for the new tower near Limerick; the tower was to be occupied by a fire warden in spring and fall
A Camp Stoney Creek enrollee was hurt cutting brush near the Limerick fire tower (Portsmouth Times, May 24, 1935)

evidence.supports: Site is in Jackson County, Ohio
Register number US 1567, OH 13 and registration date
A new forestry tower was erected at McCune Ridge, Jackson County, in August 1934
evidence.quote: a new forestry tower has been erected at McCune Ridge, Jackson County

evidence.supports: Associate State Forester B. F. Leete announced the tower
evidence.quote: Associate State Forester B. F. Leete announced today

evidence.supports: Part of a state plan to install towers in southern Ohio forests at 15-mile intervals
evidence.quote: in furtherance of the new plan of the department of forestry to install fire towers throughout the forests of Southern Ohio at 15 mile intervals

evidence.supports: Tower 20 feet taller than the one on the Scioto trail, with an aluminum finish
evidence.quote: The new tower is 20 feet higher than the one on the Scioto trail and is coated with an aluminum finish.

evidence.supports: Federal funds paid for the project; CCC camp labor under Henry B. Sherman
evidence.quote: The project was completed with funds furnished by the federal government, and labor from the CCC camps under the supervision of Henry B. Sherman.

evidence.supports: Tower to be occupied by a fire warden in spring and fall
evidence.quote: It will be occupied during the spring and fall by a fire warden.

evidence.supports: Allen Weese named as observer for the tower near Limerick, October 1934
evidence.quote: Mr. Allen Weese will act as observer on the new McCune Ridge tower near Limerick in Jackson Co.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page lists the agency as Wayne National Forest
A Camp Stoney Creek enrollee was hurt in May 1935 near the Limerick fire tower
The Limerick tower is placed in Liberty township
evidence.quote: near the Limerick fire tower in Liberty township, Jackson county

evidence.supports: Limerick is an unincorporated community in Jackson Township, which disagrees with the 1935 township
evidence.quote: Limerick is an unincorporated community in Jackson Township

evidence.supports: The national forest was first established in 1935, after the tower was built
evidence.quote: The national forest was originally established in 1935 with the first land acquisitions.

evidence.supports: Ohio list marks the tower as gone; register number US 1567, OH 13
evidence.quote: McCune (Limerick) Jackson 39.10007 -82.73635 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1567, OH 13

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts page lists Wayne National Forest, but the 1934 report credits the state forestry department with federal funds, and Wikipedia gives the national forest's first establishment as 1935, after the tower was built. The story reports both
A 1935 report places the tower in Liberty Township; Wikipedia places the community of Limerick in Jackson Township. Both may be true of different points, but the sources do not say so

notes_for_editor: Three 1934-1935 newspaper items from the Forest Lookouts page support the build and staffing sentences; they are plans and announcements, not service records. Agency and township are contested as noted. Gone status rests on the Ohio list; no removal date or present-day description found. Only one search for present-day site condition; a ridge photo search could be worth a later pass.
